# Microsoft Store listing material

The editable listing text for the three products lives in
[listings.json](listings.json): **GPROXY Desktop** (desktop application),
**GPROXY CLI** (terminal with browser console) and **GPROXY Headless**
(terminal without the web console). All three are published by **Leen Hawk**
under AGPL-3.0-or-later.

Desktop and CLI have English, Russian, Simplified Chinese and Traditional
Chinese listings; Headless has English, Simplified Chinese and Traditional
Chinese. The Russian listings were added to the Store entries only: packages
published before that declare `en-us`, `zh-cn` and `zh-tw` resources, and
packages built from the current `scripts/package-windows-msix.ps1` also
declare `ru-ru`. Partner Center holds the submitted text; keep this file in
step with it when either changes.

Use [PRIVACY.md](../../PRIVACY.md) for the privacy information. Website:
<https://gproxy.leenhawk.com/>. Support:
<https://github.com/LeenHawk/gproxy/issues>, or privately at <leenhawk@leenhawk.com>.

Descriptions and feature lists are independent of release versions. The Store
publisher reads the selected GitHub release's version, notes and URL at runtime
and updates each listing's release notes before committing the submission.
It preserves the other listing text, screenshots and publishing settings.

## Desktop certification notes

GPROXY Desktop is a native Rust/Tauri developer tool with an embedded WebView2
management window. The setup wizard selects the data directory and listening
address and creates a local administrator. The gateway listens on loopback by
default and forwards authorized API requests to providers configured by the
user. Management remains in the application window; the HTTP port is for API
clients and does not expose the desktop console.

`runFullTrust` is required for the native process, local HTTP listener, selected
storage backends and operating-system credential store. The application does
not require elevation or install a system service. The user can enable a
Windows StartupTask. Store-installed copies obtain updates through Microsoft
Store. No PowerShell setup helper is used by the Tauri application.

## CLI certification notes

GPROXY CLI is a native console developer tool. Open PowerShell or Windows
Terminal and run `gproxy --help`, then start an instance with:

```powershell
gproxy serve --data-dir "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\GPROXY" --port 8787
```

Save the administrator credentials printed at first startup and open
<http://127.0.0.1:8787/console/>. The account and management interface work
without a paid model account. To test actual model requests, configure the
reviewer's own supported provider account; no provider subscription is bundled.
Set a persistent `GPROXY_MASTER_KEY` before adding upstream credentials when
encrypted credential storage is needed.

`runFullTrust` is required for the console executable, local HTTP listener and
configured data storage. The `gproxy.exe` app execution alias makes the command
available to the user's terminal. No elevation, system service or automatic
login startup is installed by the CLI package. Store updates are handled by
Microsoft Store.

## Headless certification notes

GPROXY Headless is the CLI without the web console, packaged with its own
identity and the `gproxy-headless.exe` app execution alias, so it can be
installed next to GPROXY CLI without taking over `gproxy.exe`. Open PowerShell
or Windows Terminal and run `gproxy-headless --help`, then start an instance:

```powershell
gproxy-headless serve --data-dir "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\GPROXY" --port 8787
```

Save the administrator credentials printed at first startup;
<http://127.0.0.1:8787/healthz> answers while the instance runs. There is no
browser console: configuration uses the command line and the management API.
The same no-provider-account and `GPROXY_MASTER_KEY` notes as for the CLI
apply, and so do its `runFullTrust`, no-elevation, no-service and
Store-update statements.

## Content and screenshots

All three editions are developer gateways, not model providers or content catalogs.
They can display responses generated by user-selected providers from user
prompts. Provider moderation policies vary; GPROXY does not promise to filter
all generated content. Disclose this in the generative-AI declaration and
certification notes. They do not bundle age-restricted media, advertising,
social messaging, gambling or digital purchases.

Capture current application screens from isolated demonstration instances.
Never include actual API credentials, personal request logs or account details.
Do not reuse screenshots of the old browser-launching desktop host. Screenshot
captions should identify the desktop window, CLI browser console or Headless
terminal output accurately.
